papers.title: Impact of AlN buffer thickness on electrical and thermal characteristics of AlGaN/GaN/AlN HEMTs
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of AlN buffer thickness on the structural, electrical, and thermal properties of AlGaN/GaN high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) grown on semi-insulating SiC substrates by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition. X-ray diffraction and atomic force microscopy reveal that while thin AlN layers (120 nm) exhibit compressive strain and smooth step-flow surfaces, thicker single-layer buffers (550 nm) develop tensile strain and increased surface roughness. Multi-layer buffer structures up to 2 μm alleviate strain and maintain surface integrity. Low-temperature Hall measurements confirm that electron mobility decreases with increasing interface roughness, with the highest mobility observed in the structure with a thin AlN buffer. Transient thermoreflectance measurements show that thermal conductivity (ThC) of the AlN buffer increases with the thickness, reaching 188 W/m.K at 300 K for the 2 μm buffer layer, which is approximately 60% of the bulk AlN ThC value. These results highlight the importance of optimizing AlN buffer design to balance strain relaxation, thermal management, and carrier transport for high-performance GaN-based HEMTs.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究AlN缓冲层厚度对GaN基HEMT性能的影响
summary_zh.method: MOCVD生长不同厚度AlN缓冲层，结合XRD、AFM、霍尔和热反射测量
summary_zh.result: 薄缓冲层具有更高迁移率，厚缓冲层热导率提升但表面粗糙度增加
summary_zh.validation: 实验测量验证结构和电热性能

summary_en.motivation: Investigate the effect of AlN buffer thickness on the electrical and thermal properties of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs.
summary_en.method: Grew AlN buffers of varying thickness by MOCVD and characterized structural, electrical, and thermal properties using XRD, AFM, Hall, and transient thermoreflectance.
summary_en.result: Thin buffers yield higher electron mobility while thick buffers achieve higher thermal conductivity up to 188 W/m.K.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements validate the trade-off between mobility and thermal conductivity.
